title: Effects of Heat Input on the Stability of the Sigma Phase in Super Duplex Stainless Steel UNS S32750
content: Super duplex stainless steels (SDSS) combine excellent mechanical strength and corrosion resistance but may undergo microstructural degradation when exposed to temperatures between 400 and 1010 °C, due to the precipitation of deleterious intermetallic phases such as the sigma (σ) phase. This study investigates the phase evolution in UNS S32750 SDSS subjected to aging treatments at 850, 900, and 950 °C for 10, 100, and 1000 min, followed by water quenching and furnace cooling. The surface and phase microhardness, as well as the volume fraction and average grain size of the σ-phase, were evaluated. The results showed an increase in microhardness with both temperature and aging time, reaching a maximum of 418 ± 4 HV₀.₅ under the 850 °C / 1000 min condition. The σ-phase volume fraction remained nearly constant after 1000 min, regardless of the cooling method, while grain growth exhibited a similar trend across the three evaluated temperatures. These findings enhance the understanding of σ-phase precipitation and dissolution mechanisms and provide valuable insights for defining optimal thermal parameters in welding and manufacturing processes involving UNS S32750 super duplex stainless steel.
